payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge. The battery delivers 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density. Projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. Its negative-electrolyte dopant precipitates below 4 °C, requiring cycling to stop in colder conditions.
